$comment: REQ-THM-041 fixtures for pipeline step 5. `ratio` is the WCAG 2.2 contrast ratio, computed to 4 decimal places from the sRGB relative-luminance formula, and both engines MUST agree to 3 decimals — an engine that rounds differently would accept a theme the other rejects and break REQ-GEN-031. Thresholds: 4.5 for normal text, 3.0 for large text, where large means >=18.66 px regular or >=14 px bold. At the design-system default scale only `display` (34 px) and `headline` (24 px) are large, so `title` at 18 px is judged as normal text despite reading as a heading — see design-system/typography.md. `verdict` is the DEFAULT behaviour: below the floor is accept-with-warning, because REQ-THM-041 makes rejection conditional on the user enabling 'Enforce accessible contrast' (default off, forced on by the high-contrast theme and by the OS high-contrast setting). `enforcedVerdict` is what the same pair produces once that switch is on. A theme is never rejected for contrast by default; recording both columns is what keeps the requirement from being read as one or the other.
alphaHandling: The ratio is computed on the RGB channels, alpha ignored. Compositing the foreground over its actual backdrop would be more accurate but is not computable at validation time: the backdrop depends on which surface the text lands on and on assets.backgroundOpacity. Ignoring alpha is therefore the conservative, deterministic choice, and it is a documented narrowing of REQ-THM-041 rather than an oversight — logged in docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md.

pairs.why: Anchor: the maximum ratio is exactly 21.
Order must not matter — the formula is symmetric.
theme-full primary text on base background.
theme-full secondary text on base background.
Tertiary text: the tightest passing pair in theme-full.
onAccent over accent — the pair skins get wrong most often.
Just over the 4.5 floor; the classic AA boundary grey.
One step darker, still passing — brackets the boundary.
One step lighter: FAILS AA for normal text.
Grey on grey: fails both floors.
Same colours judged as large text: still fails.
Passes the 3:1 large-text floor but not the 4.5 normal floor — the pair that proves the two thresholds are applied per type style, not per theme.
Alpha in the foreground. The ratio below IGNORES alpha and uses the RGB channels only.
